name: a-two-colour-overhead
prompt: A tall portrait illustration printed like a plate from a 1919 weekly magazine, two inks only on cream newsprint: dense black ink line and one flat, unshaded patch of brick red, with no other colour anywhere. The view drops straight down from the top of a cast-iron park lamp, high above a single slatted wooden bench in a bare winter park. The gravel path, the bench and the long blue-black shadows of leafless trees run as one hard diagonal from the lower left corner to the upper right. On the left end of the bench sits a huge, round, well-fed gentleman seen from above: the crown of a tall silk hat, broad black frock-coat shoulders, a white starched collar, and a tight waistcoat that is the only red thing in the picture, its flat red sprinkled with tiny printed dollar signs. His gloved right hand is flung out wide, palm turned away, brushing the air off to the side as if shooing a fly. At the far right end, as much empty slat between them as the bench allows, a gaunt young soldier in a worn greatcoat and peaked cap sits hunched with one trouser leg folded and pinned at the knee, a single laced army boot planted on the gravel, a wooden crutch leaning against the armrest; the low sun stretches the crutch and the lone boot into thin, separate black shadows across the path. Drawn in confident pen strokes with parallel hatching for the shadows and solid black fills for coats and hat, the red laid flat inside its own edge without an outline, the paper slightly toothy with faint ink spread. The top fifth of the frame is plain, empty off-white paper margin with nothing drawn in it. No letters, words, signatures or speech balloons anywhere in the image. Thanks.
